That changes it. VARCHAR and TEXT both use varlena storage in Postgres, with identical read performance. The only difference is VARCHAR enforces a length constraint at write time; TEXT doesn't. The length check adds no read cost.

Choose based on the constraint you want, not performance. If you need to reject values over 2000 chars, use VARCHAR(2000). If the length is unbounded or you don't care about enforcement, use TEXT.
